title: The Best Small Towns in Florida to Live or Retire Near the Water
dek: Nine Florida towns under 30,000 people with a real downtown you can walk, the water close by, and no strip mall sprawl, from a $350K fishing town to Amelia Island.
body:
The best small towns in Florida to live or retire near the water are Fernandina Beach, Venice and Apalachicola. Each has fewer than 30,000 year round residents, a historic downtown you can walk, and the beach or bay a short trip away. Apalachicola is the most affordable, with a typical home around $350K.

A lot of Florida "small towns" turn out to be suburbs with a beach exit. We looked for the real thing: a town under 30,000 people in the 2020 Census, with a walkable center on our scoring (4 out of 5 or better, with one exception we explain), its own character, and water at the end of the street. Nine made the cut. We also list the honest catch, because in Florida small usually means farther from airports, hospitals or both, which matters most if you are retiring.

Population is the 2020 Census count for each city. Prices are the typical figures on our town pages. Hospital and airport distances are from our town data.

1. Fernandina Beach

A Victorian era downtown on Centre Street, shrimp boats at the marina, and wide, uncrowded Atlantic beaches on the same island. It scores a 5 out of 5 for walkability, has a hospital about a mile from downtown, and Jacksonville's airport is about 40 minutes away, which is rare for a town this size. A typical home is about $658K. The catch: Amelia Island is a barrier island, so storm surge is the risk to check on any house.

2. Venice

The biggest town on our list at about 25,000 people, but it still feels small: a walkable historic downtown, Venice Avenue running to the Gulf, a jetty for sunsets and bike trails out of town. A typical home is about $495K, and there is more house for the money on the mainland side. The catch: it is busy in winter, and quiet at night.

3. Apalachicola

About 2,300 people, brick storefronts, oyster history and a working waterfront on Apalachicola Bay. You can walk to breakfast past the shrimp boats and drive over the bridge to the beaches of St. George Island. A typical home is about $350K, among the lowest of any town we score. The catch: Tallahassee's airport is about an hour and a half away, and the nearest trauma center is about 50 miles off, which matters for retirees.

4. Stuart

A charming riverfront downtown with a walkable main street, serious fishing, and Stuart Beach on Hutchinson Island just over the bridge. It also has the lowest flood score of any town in our flood rankings, 1.5 out of 10. A typical home is about $452K. The catch: Lake Okeechobee releases can foul the St. Lucie River some summers, and Palm Beach's airport is about 45 minutes away.

5. Tarpon Springs

A town with real Greek roots, the historic Sponge Docks, bakeries and a walkable downtown, plus Fred Howard Park's beach on the Gulf. Tampa's airport is about 40 minutes away and there is a hospital in town. A typical home is about $448K. The catch: tourist traffic at the docks, and Hurricane Helene's surge flooded the Sponge Docks in 2024, so check flood zones near the bayous.

6. Punta Gorda

A pretty, walkable harbor town with a waterfront trail, canal homes with boat access, and its own airport about 10 minutes from downtown. It is one of the best picks on this list for boaters. A typical home is about $588K. The catch: the Gulf beaches are about 40 minutes away, and downtown flooded in Ian in 2022 and again in 2024.

7. Port St. Joe

A small town on calm, clear St. Joseph Bay, with the beaches of Cape San Blas a short drive out and almost no nightlife. A typical home is about $425K. It is our one exception on walkability, scoring 3 out of 5: the town center is small and walkable, but most errands mean a short drive. The catch: the nearest big airport is about an hour away, and Hurricane Michael hit hard here in 2018.

8. Gulfport

An arty little waterfront town of about 12,000 people right next to St. Petersburg, with galleries and live music on Beach Boulevard and a small bay beach. It is the best pick if you want small town life with a city and an airport next door. A typical home is about $450K. The catch: Gulfport is low lying, and Helene flooded many streets in 2024.

9. Cedar Key

The smallest town on our list, with fewer than 700 residents on a cluster of Gulf islands, clam farms, kayaking through the backwater keys and some of the quietest nights in Florida. A typical home is about $375K. The catch: services are thin. The nearest full grocery store is about 40 minutes away, the nearest hospital about 28 miles, and recent hurricanes hit the island hard.

Which small Florida town is best for retirees?

If health care is high on your list, look first at towns with a hospital within a few miles and a real airport within an hour: Fernandina Beach, Venice, Stuart, Tarpon Springs and Punta Gorda all fit. Apalachicola, Port St. Joe and Cedar Key are wonderful places to live, but plan on longer drives for specialists. For more towns with the same feel, see the best towns for Old Florida charm and the most walkable beach towns.

What to know before you move to a small Florida town

  • Visit in August. Small towns that buzz in March can be very quiet in summer. Make sure you like both.
  • Check flood and storm history street by street. Most of these towns grew up on the water, which is the charm and the risk.
  • Price insurance before you fall in love. See what homeowners insurance costs by county.
  • Ask locals about year round life. Which restaurants stay open in the off season, and where people actually shop, tells you a lot.
faq: What is the best small town in Florida to live in near the beach?
Fernandina Beach on Amelia Island is our top pick: about 13,000 residents, a walkable historic downtown, a hospital in town and Jacksonville's airport about 40 minutes away.
What is the cheapest small beach town in Florida?
Of the towns on this list, Apalachicola on the Forgotten Coast has the lowest typical home price, about $350K.
What small Florida towns are good for retirees?
Fernandina Beach, Venice, Stuart, Tarpon Springs and Punta Gorda each combine a walkable downtown with a hospital within about 5 miles and an airport within about 45 minutes.
Are there small towns in Florida that still feel like Old Florida?
Yes. Apalachicola, Cedar Key and Port St. Joe are the most Old Florida towns on this list: working waterfronts, little new development and quiet nights.
